results.score_rationale: Platform fundamentals pass (HTTPS + 301s, self-canonicals, SSR, real 404s, current Shopify robots.txt, valid sitemaps), but the index is structurally doubled twice (575 /ro-hu/ duplicates + 58 B2B cross-domain duplicates), six utility/empty collections and a thank-you page are indexable and in the sitemap, the 354-article blog sits behind a 59-page prev/next-only archive, and every page ships a mis-ordered 157-189 KB head with a zoom-locked viewport. Category scores: crawlability 55, indexability 35, security 80, URL structure 65, mobile 70, JS rendering 95, structured data 40, CWV not measured, IndexNow not implemented.
what_works: HTTPS enforced; http->https and www->non-www 301; primesupplements1.myshopify.com 301s to the primary domain
HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, CSP frame-ancestors 'none' on every 200 response; HTTP/2 via Cloudflare
Self-referencing canonicals on all 24 parsed pages; ?sort_by and ?filter.* canonicalise to the bare collection; ?page=N self-canonical with rel prev/next and '- Pagina N' title suffix
/search?q= served with X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
robots.txt is Shopify's current 2026 default: blocks sort_by, multi-filter, +tag combos, cart/checkout/account; sitemap declared (corrects the context file)
Unknown URLs return real HTTP 404 (title '404 negasit', no-store)
Sitemap index well-formed; 185 product entries with lastmod + image; 354 articles with lastmod over 90 distinct dates
Server-side rendering: product raw HTML has 1,039 visible words, article 2,367, collection grid 24 product cards; no SPA; no pushState/replaceState back-button hijack
html lang=ro; hreflang triplet (x-default/ro/ro-HU) consistent with return links
Googlebot and other bots excluded from Shopify's web-pixel loader; theme assets light (theme.css 27 KB, theme.js 35 KB, vendor.min.js 21 KB) as ES modules; theme fonts and theme.css preloaded
Largest HTML (617 KB) well under Googlebot's 2 MB cap; title and canonical within the first 1.5 KB
limitations: Core Web Vitals not measurable (PSI quota exhausted, no CrUX, no Chromium); CWV statements are static risk signals only
/collections/vendors?q=primesupplements1 returned Cloudflare 429 twice this session; evidence taken from the earlier capture scratchpad/tech/live/vendors.body
$R/theme/layout__theme.liquid was absent; the live layout was read via one read-only Admin GraphQL query (themes.files, theme 179784286583); nothing was modified
B2B store robots.txt/password state taken from the context file, not re-fetched
Google's rendered DOM not compared with raw HTML (render_page.py blocked by sandbox proxy)
Crawl depth derived from pagination settings and page counts, not from a crawler run
Pandectes banner intrusiveness not assessed

findings.title: The /ro-hu/ 'Ungaria' market publishes a full second copy of the site (575 duplicate URLs, self-canonical, identical Romanian content and RON prices)
findings.evidence: all-urls.txt: 1,151 URLs = 576 primary + 575 /ro-hu/ exact mirror (185 products, 23 collections, 354 articles, 11 pages). Sitemap index lists the six content sitemaps twice. Live GET /ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure -> 200, canonical https://primesupplements.ro/ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure, og:url /ro-hu/, html lang=ro, 41 RON mentions, 72 internal links all under /ro-hu/. homepage-ro-hu.html identical to home.html (2,950 words) except 175 /ro-hu/ links; its canonical is https://primesupplements.ro/ro-hu (no slash) while served at /ro-hu/. hreflang ro-HU -> /ro-hu/ on every page. Admin: hu locale unpublished, market currency null.
findings.affected_scope: 575 of 1,151 sitemap URLs plus all paginated/parameter variants (every indexable URL)
findings.recommendation: Preferred: Settings -> Markets -> Ungaria -> Domains and languages -> remove the /ro-hu subfolder web presence or deactivate the market until a translated hu locale is published (removes /ro-hu/ sitemaps, ro-HU hreflang and the duplicates at source). Fallback if the market must stay: in layout/theme.liquid compute canonical_href = canonical_url | replace_first: 'primesupplements.ro/ro-hu', 'primesupplements.ro' (normalise bare root to trailing slash) when localization.country.iso_code == 'HU', and emit <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow"> for HU.
findings.falsifiability: curl -s https://primesupplements.ro/sitemap.xml | grep -c ro-hu must be 0 and /ro-hu/... must not return a self-canonical 200; if GSC still shows /ro-hu/ URLs Indexed after 4 weeks, the fix failed
findings.leading_indicator: GSC Pages: 'Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user' and 'Alternate page with proper canonical tag' counts; crawl requests dropping ~40-50%

votes.reasoning: Reproduced exactly at audit time. With hreflang ro / ro-HU declared, this is a doubled crawl surface with confusing canonicals. It is not an indexing blocker, so the right severity is High rather than the report-level Critical. Round 2 removed the web presence and added 575 301s on 2026-10-13, and the fix holds live.
votes.evidence: all-urls.txt has 1,151 URLs: 576 primary plus 575 under /ro-hu (574 with '/ro-hu/' plus the bare /ro-hu). The audit-time sitemap index lists 6 content sitemaps twice (child7-12). live-tech/rohu_product shows a self-canonical at https://primesupplements.ro/ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure with hreflang x-default/ro/ro-HU. Live 2026-10-13: /ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure returns 301 to /products/creatina-creapure in one hop. sitemap.xml has 7 children and 0 'ro-hu'. The homepage has 0 hreflang tags and 0 '/ro-hu' links.
votes.r2_note: Live: /ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure 301 to /products/creatina-creapure; sitemap.xml has 0 ro-hu entries; homepage has no ro-HU hreflang.

votes.reasoning: Real problem at audit time: 575 self-canonical copies of the whole site with hreflang ro-HU pointing at identical Romanian pages in RON. It doubled crawl and split signals, and Google could pick a /ro-hu URL as canonical (Search Central, 'Consolidate duplicate URLs'). The report's Critical label is inflated. Under the audit's rules, Critical means blocking indexing or eligibility. Duplicates are not penalised, Google consolidates them, and a ro-HU alternate is technically valid hreflang, so High is the right level. The preferred fix (delete the web presence, then 1:1 301s) is the correct and safe Shopify approach. URL redirects fire only after the path 404s, which it now does. Falsifiability is measurable. Fixed in round 2 and verified live. Keep the 575 redirects for at least a year, as Google advises for site moves.
votes.evidence: curl 2026-10-13: HTTP/2 301 location /products/creatina-creapure; grep -c ro-hu sitemap.xml = 0
votes.corrected_recommendation: Mark as fixed (R2). Keep the redirects for at least 12 months. Deactivate the Ungaria market, or remove it from the selector, so customers in HU are not served a market without a web presence. In GSC, watch for /ro-hu URLs moving to 'Page with redirect'.
votes.r2_note: Live 2026-10-13: /ro-hu/products/creatina-creapure returns 301 to /products/creatina-creapure, and sitemap.xml has 0 ro-hu entries (6 child sitemaps + agentic). Still open: INTERNATIONAL-05 (the Ungaria market still appears in the country selector) and the HU shipping zone.

verification.corrected_recommendation: Mark as fixed (R2). Keep the redirects for at least 12 months. Deactivate the Ungaria market, or remove it from the selector, so customers in HU are not served a market without a web presence. In GSC, watch for /ro-hu URLs moving to 'Page with redirect'.

findings.title: The B2B store b2b.primesupplements.ro is an indexable cross-domain duplicate of the product catalogue (58 same-handle product URLs)
findings.evidence: b2b-products-sitemap.xml lists 58 <loc> with the same handles as the main store (/products/baton-proteic-capsuni, /products/creatina-creapure...). b2b-product.html: canonical https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/creatina-creapure (self), no meta robots, no hreflang, 0 links to primesupplements.ro, title 'Creatina (Creapure) 500g/100 serv - PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL / 46260823'. b2b.html 940 KB, title 'PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL / 46260823'. Context: B2B robots.txt Shopify default, no password.
findings.affected_scope: 58 product pages (core supplements range) + B2B home/collections
findings.recommendation: (a) Enable the storefront password on the B2B store (Online Store -> Preferences -> Restrict access), which 302s every URL to /password and withdraws the sitemap; or (b) add <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> to its layout/theme.liquid plus templates/robots.txt.liquid with Disallow: /, and rename the store from 'PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL / 46260823' to 'Prime Supplements B2B'. Do not use cross-domain canonicals to the retail store.
findings.falsifiability: curl -sI https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/creatina-creapure returns 302 to /password or contains noindex; if site:b2b.primesupplements.ro still returns product pages after 6 weeks, the fix failed
findings.leading_indicator: site:b2b.primesupplements.ro result count trending to 0; main-store GSC no longer listing b2b URLs as Google-selected canonical

votes.reasoning: The B2B store is indexable and self-canonical, but the count is overstated. Its sitemap has 58 <loc> entries: 1 homepage plus 57 product URLs. Of the 57, 52 share a handle with the main store, so '58 same-handle product URLs' should read 52. The page has no meta robots, its title is the company name, and it has 0 links to the main domain. Fixing it is still an owner action.
votes.evidence: pages/b2b-products-sitemap.xml: 58 locs, 57 /products/, and 52 handles also present in main child1.xml. b2b-product.html: title 'Creatina (Creapure®) 500g/100 serv – PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL / 46260823', no noindex, 0 href to https://primesupplements.ro.

votes.reasoning: The cross-domain duplicate is real: same handles and, at audit time, the same product copy, indexable on a subdomain titled with the legal entity name. Round 2 rewrote the retail descriptions on all 195 products, so the retail pages are no longer verbatim copies. What remains is name-level competition and a wholesale storefront that can surface in brand and product SERPs, which is Medium rather than High. No evidence was collected that Google actually selects the B2B URLs. The recommendation has two safety problems. (1) Option (b) pairs noindex with robots.txt 'Disallow: /'. Google's noindex documentation says the page must not be blocked by robots.txt or the noindex is never seen, so URLs already indexed can stay as 'Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt'. (2) A storefront password (Online Store > Preferences > Password protection) locks out every visitor, including the existing B2B customers who use the store with login-gated pricing. That is a business side effect the owner must accept explicitly.
votes.evidence: Live curl 2026-10-13: HTTP/2 200, no x-robots-tag, no <meta name=robots> in b2b product HTML.
votes.corrected_recommendation: Step 1: in the B2B theme's layout/theme.liquid add <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">. Keep robots.txt crawlable until site:b2b.primesupplements.ro returns nothing. Optionally speed this up with GSC Removals on a Domain property. Step 2, only after de-indexing: either keep it as is, or gate the catalogue behind customer login with the B2B app ('require login to view store'), which leaves the login page reachable for B2B clients. Use the storefront password only if every B2B customer can be given it. Do not use cross-domain canonicals. Rename the store to 'Prime Supplements B2B'.
votes.r2_note: Still PENDING (owner). Live b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/creatina-creapure returns 200 with no x-robots-tag and no meta robots.

findings.title: Five utility collections (all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva, frontpage) are indexable and in the sitemap, three of them full-catalogue duplicates of each other; the theme has no robots-meta logic at all
findings.evidence: sitemaps/child3.xml lists /collections/all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva, frontpage (+ /ro-hu/ twins in child9.xml). parsed/pages_collection-all.json: title 'All Products', H1 'All Products', canonical self, no meta robots, pagination '1 / 8' (products_per_page 24). Admin: all / cele-mai-vandute / lansate-recent each contain all 185 active products in a different order; 11-tva is an internal VAT grouping (15 products, title '11% TVA'); frontpage holds 1 product; 8/23 collections have no SEO title/description, all have empty descriptions. Live layout/theme.liquid contains no <meta name="robots"> logic (only <link rel="canonical" href="{{ canonical_url }}">).
findings.affected_scope: 5 collections x up to 8 paginated pages x 2 markets = up to ~80 listing URLs re-listing the same 185 products
findings.recommendation: No-code: Settings -> Custom data -> Collections -> definition namespace seo, key hidden, type Integer; set 1 on all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva, frontpage, reduceri (Shopify injects noindex and removes the URL from the sitemap). Belt-and-braces: add to layout/theme.liquid after the canonical a {%- liquid -%} block that sets seo_noindex when request.page_type == 'collection' and (utility handle list contains collection.handle, or collection.handle == 'vendors'/'types', or current_tags.size > 0, or collection.products_count == 0), when request.page_type == 'blog' and current_tags.size > 0, when page.handle == 'thank-you', and when request.page_type == 'search'; then output <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">. Keep /collections/all as the user hub (noindex, follow) and make category collections the indexable listings.
findings.falsifiability: curl -s https://primesupplements.ro/collections/all | grep -c noindex = 1 and the sitemap no longer lists it; if GSC still shows /collections/cele-mai-vandute Indexed after a recrawl, the fix did not apply
findings.leading_indicator: GSC 'Excluded by noindex tag' rising by the number of utility URLs; impressions moving from /collections/all?page=N to category collections

votes.reasoning: The facts are true: utility collections are in the sitemap, are self-canonical, and the live theme has no robots meta at all. The listing-URL scope is inflated, though. The real count is all, cele-mai-vandute and lansate-recent at 8 pages each, plus 11-tva and frontpage at 1 page each: 26 per market, 52 at audit time, 26 after /ro-hu was removed. The specialist said 'up to ~80'. Utility and all-products collections are standard on Shopify and rarely hurt rankings materially, so Medium rather than High. The noindex exists only in the staging theme (READY), so this is not fixed live.
votes.evidence: child3.xml and child9.xml both list all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, reduceri, 11-tva and frontpage. collection-all.html shows pagination '1 / 8'. Live theme layout__theme.liquid has only <link rel=canonical> and no robots logic. theme-fixes/layout/theme.liquid has a utility_collections noindex list.

votes.reasoning: Valid index-quality issue: three full-catalogue listings plus a VAT grouping, all indexable. Calling it High is inflated. The site has about 600 URLs, and Google says crawl budget only matters for very large or fast-changing sites (1M+ pages, or 10k+ changing daily). Duplicate listings are consolidated, not penalised. The impact is that the wrong listing can rank for generic queries, so Medium. The staging Liquid is valid ('array contains string', current_tags) and safe. However, a theme meta noindex does not remove the URLs from sitemap.xml. Once published, GSC will report 'Submitted URL marked noindex' for 6 URLs. The specialist's no-code route, the seo.hidden metafield, removes them from the sitemap and injects noindex, but Shopify's injected tag is noindex,nofollow. That is acceptable here because every product is also linked from category collections and the sitemap. It is a data-only change, so it is compatible with the owner's no-design rule and can be applied before the theme publish. Falsifiability is measurable (grep noindex plus absence from the sitemap).
votes.evidence: Live sitemap_collections_1.xml (2026-10-13) still contains /collections/all, /cele-mai-vandute, /lansate-recent, /11-tva, /frontpage, /reduceri.
votes.corrected_recommendation: Set the seo.hidden = 1 metafield (integer) now on all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva and frontpage. This removes them from the sitemap and adds noindex without any theme change. Keep the staging noindex,follow block as a belt-and-braces measure. Do not hard-code 'reduceri' (see TECH-05). Use 'collection.products_count == 0' instead, so the page becomes indexable again once it has products.
votes.r2_note: The staging theme.liquid contains the utility_collections noindex block (verified in theme-fixes/layout/theme.liquid). The live sitemap_collections_1.xml still lists all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva, frontpage and reduceri.

verification.corrected_recommendation: Set the seo.hidden = 1 metafield (integer) now on all, cele-mai-vandute, lansate-recent, 11-tva and frontpage. This removes them from the sitemap and adds noindex without any theme change. Keep the staging noindex,follow block as a belt-and-braces measure. Do not hard-code 'reduceri' (see TECH-05). Use 'collection.products_count == 0' instead, so the page becomes indexable again once it has products.

findings.title: Blog archive is 59 pages deep with prev/next-only pagination (6 articles per page): most of the 354 articles are 20-59 clicks from any hub
findings.evidence: blog-index.html pagination__current '1 / 59', 11 distinct article links, only href="/blogs/news?page=2" as pagination links; snippets/pagination.liquid renders only paginate.previous/next (no paginate.parts); sections/main-blog.liquid articles_per_page min 5 / max 24 / default 6; 354 articles -> ceil(354/6) = 59 pages. 346/355 articles untagged (5 tags), no tag hubs; homepage links only to the blog index. rel=next present but unused by Google since 2019. Collections share the same snippet (/collections/all 8 pages, /collections/haine-mnx 4).
findings.affected_scope: ~340 of 354 articles (everything beyond page 2) + paginated collections
findings.recommendation: 1) Theme editor -> Blog -> Articles per page = 24 (15 pages). 2) Add numbered links in snippets/pagination.liquid using {%- for part in paginate.parts -%} (link when part.is_link, aria-current span for the current page). 3) Tag the articles into 8-12 topic tags and link /blogs/news/tagged/<tag> hubs from the blog index and a related-articles block in sections/main-article.liquid; add 3-5 related-article links on product pages. 4) Add an HTML sitemap page (/pages/harta-site) linked from sections/footer.liquid.
findings.falsifiability: A crawl depth report shows max click depth from / <= 5 for all /blogs/news/* URLs; URLs still at depth > 10 mean failure
findings.leading_indicator: GSC 'Crawled - currently not indexed' and 'Discovered - currently not indexed' counts for /blogs/news/ URLs; crawl frequency of deep articles

votes.reasoning: Reproduced: 354 articles at 6 per page gives 59 pages, and pagination.liquid renders only previous/next links. That puts about 234 articles (pages 21-59) 20 or more clicks deep through pagination. Every article is in the sitemap, so this is a link-equity and crawl-depth optimisation, not a ranking blocker: Medium. After round 2 consolidation the live archive is 121 articles across 21 pages. The pagination itself was left alone under the DESIGN rule.
votes.evidence: blog-index.html shows pagination__current '1 / 59' and the only page link is ?page=2. snippets__pagination.liquid uses only paginate.previous and paginate.next. In main-blog.liquid, articles_per_page defaults to 6 (min 5, max 24). Live 2026-10-13 /blogs/news shows pagination '1/21'.

votes.reasoning: Depth was real at audit time (59 prev/next pages). Google's ecommerce pagination guidance only requires sequential <a href> links on unique URLs, which existed, and every article was in the sitemap. So this was a link-equity and importance problem, not a discovery or indexing block. Medium, not High. Round 2 cut the archive to 21 pages, added tag hub links on the blog index and collection-to-guide links, which removes most of the depth. The recommendation is technically valid: paginate.parts is standard Liquid and articles_per_page is a section setting. Both change the visible page, so under the owner's rule they are design decisions. The HTML sitemap page is low value. The recommendation also conflicts with TECH-08's noindex on blog tag pages, which the staging theme applies, while the tag pages are now the hub navigation (see TECH-08). Falsifiability (crawl-depth report) is measurable.
votes.evidence: Live /blogs/news: pagination__current '1 / 21'; tagged links such as /blogs/news/tagged/hub-aminoacizi, /creatina, /crema-de-orez.
votes.corrected_recommendation: Treat the depth problem as largely solved by consolidation (121 articles) plus the tag hubs and collection guide blocks. After the theme publish, verify that every article is within 3 clicks of a hub tag page or a collection. Raise articles_per_page or add numbered pagination only if the owner accepts the visual change. Never use hidden links. Decide whether the hub-* tag pages stay indexable (unique title from current_tags) or noindex,follow (see TECH-08).
votes.r2_note: Live blog index now shows '1 / 21' (121 articles after consolidation) and links about 20 /blogs/news/tagged/* hub URLs. Hub article blocks on collections are READY-R2. Numbered pagination was left as DESIGN.

verification.corrected_recommendation: Treat the depth problem as largely solved by consolidation (121 articles) plus the tag hubs and collection guide blocks. After the theme publish, verify that every article is within 3 clicks of a hub tag page or a collection. Raise articles_per_page or add numbered pagination only if the owner accepts the visual change. Never use hidden links. Decide whether the hub-* tag pages stay indexable (unique title from current_tags) or noindex,follow (see TECH-08).

findings.title: Empty 'Reduceri' collection is a 200, indexable, in both sitemaps (soft-404 candidate)
findings.evidence: parsed/pages_collection-reduceri.json: title 'Reduceri', H1 'Reduceri', canonical self, 400 words of header/footer boilerplate, 0 product cards; listed in sitemaps child3.xml and child9.xml; work/hu-reduceri.html confirms the /ro-hu/ twin. Admin: 0 products, no SEO title/description. 144 of 185 products carry compare-at prices.
findings.affected_scope: 2 URLs, linked from navigation on every page
findings.recommendation: Turn it into an automated collection (condition 'Compare at price > 0' -> 144 discounted products) with a 150-word description and SEO title 'Reduceri suplimente | Prime Supplements', or set seo.hidden = 1 until it has products; the collection.products_count == 0 branch of the TECHNICAL-03 block covers it automatically.
findings.falsifiability: GSC URL inspection shows Indexed with products or Excluded by noindex; 'Soft 404' means neither fix applied
findings.leading_indicator: GSC Pages 'Soft 404' count

votes.reasoning: The empty, indexable Reduceri collection is real. The claim that it is 'linked from navigation on every page' is false. There is no href to /collections/reduceri in home.html, product.html or collection.html; the word 'Reduceri' appears only as a homepage section H2. That leaves one soft-404 candidate discoverable mainly through the sitemap, which is Low. Its noindex is staged only, and the collection rule was deliberately left for Omnibus reasons.
votes.evidence: collection-reduceri.html has 0 <product-card>. It is listed in child3.xml and child9.xml. grep 'href="[^"]*reduceri' returns 0 in home.html, product.html and collection.html.

votes.reasoning: One empty URL is a soft-404 candidate (Google's soft 404 documentation covers empty category pages). It affects UX because it is in the navigation, but it is one URL, not an optimisation affecting many pages, so Low. The recommendation's main option is unsafe. An automated 'compare-at price > 0' rule would list about 120 products whose compare-at prices are permanent as 'Reduceri'. Under the EU Omnibus price-indication rules (Directive 2019/2161, art. 6a of Directive 98/6/EC) a reduction must reference the lowest price of the previous 30 days, so this is a legal risk. Round 2 correctly refused it. The staging hard-codes 'reduceri' as noindex, which would keep the page noindexed even after real promotions are added.
votes.corrected_recommendation: While the collection is empty, set seo.hidden = 1 (data-only) or rely on a 'collection.products_count == 0' noindex branch instead of the hard-coded handle. Remove the menu item until there are genuine, Omnibus-compliant promotions, then fill it manually.
votes.r2_note: 'reduceri' is in the staging utility_collections noindex list. The collection rule change was deliberately not applied (Omnibus risk). The live sitemap still lists /collections/reduceri.

verification.corrected_recommendation: While the collection is empty, set seo.hidden = 1 (data-only) or rely on a 'collection.products_count == 0' noindex branch instead of the hard-coded handle. Remove the menu item until there are genuine, Omnibus-compliant promotions, then fill it manually.

findings.title: Shopify's automatic vendor/type pseudo-collections are live, indexable and self-canonical (/collections/vendors?q=primesupplements1, /collections/types?q=)

findings.title: <meta charset> is the third element of <head> (byte 1,078, after a synchronous external script and a JSON-LD block), breaking the 1,024-byte rule
findings.evidence: Live layout/theme.liquid head order: {% render 'schema-organization' %}, <script src="{{ 'pandectes-rules.js' | file_url }}"></script>, <meta charset="utf-8">, viewport. Rendered on all 13 main-store pages: first element <script type="application/ld+json"> (~1 KB), pandectes-rules.js at byte 1,022 (synchronous, no defer/async), <meta charset> at byte 1,078; on article-thin-lcarnitine.html the charset is at byte 2,254 because an app injects another script ahead of it. The sync script blocks parsing of title, canonical, viewport and CSS preloads.
findings.recommendation: Reorder layout/theme.liquid: <meta charset>, <meta viewport>, theme-color, <title>, description, canonical, then the Pandectes script (keep synchronous only if blocking mode is required, else defer; it must still precede content_for_header), then {% render 'schema-organization' %} at the end of head.

findings.leading_indicator: Lighthouse best-practices 'charset' audit and lower 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' estimate

What remains real is the synchronous pandectes-rules.js ahead of title and canonical, which is a parsing and performance cost. Low. The reorder is staged (READY).

The real cost is a synchronous external script parsed before <title>/canonical/CSS preloads, which is a small render-blocking performance cost: Low. votes.reasoning: Valid accessibility issue (WCAG 1.4.4). It is not a Google Search signal: the Mobile Usability report and Mobile-Friendly Test were retired in Dec 2023, and page experience covers CWV and HTTPS, not zoom. So Low, not Medium. The claim that width=device-width, initial-scale=1 is 'Impact's default' looks wrong: the current line is the stock viewport of the Maestrooo themes (Impact/Prestige/Focal). Android users gain pinch-zoom.

If it does, set those inputs to 16px on mobile, which is a minimal CSS change and needs owner approval.

findings.title: Sitemap lastmod churn: all 185 products and 21/23 collections carry today's identical timestamp
findings.evidence: sitemaps/child1.xml: 185/185 product <lastmod> = 2026-10-12T17:33:42+03:00 (one identical value); child3.xml: 21 of 23 collections 2026-10-12. Articles healthy (354 entries, 90 distinct dates). Shopify derives lastmod from updated_at, so an app/sync is touching every product daily and the signal is worthless to Google.
findings.recommendation: Identify the writer via Admin activity / Admin API events on one product (inventory sync, BSS B2B pricing, Koala); make syncs write only on change. Verify next day's sitemap spreads lastmod values again.

findings.leading_indicator: GSC Crawl stats 'By purpose: refresh' share for product URLs

votes.reasoning: The symptom is true but the diagnosis is wrong. Product updatedAt in products-all.json had 169 distinct values, while the sitemap showed one identical lastmod for all 185 products. A live re-fetch shows all 185 at 06:26:32+03:00, about one minute before the response Date header. Product sitemap lastmod is therefore the sitemap generation time, not an app sync touching products daily. The recommendation to hunt the writer in Admin activity is misdirected: this is platform behaviour the merchant cannot change. The report-level title already corrected this.
votes.evidence: Audit time: child1.xml had 185/185 at 2026-10-12T17:33:42+03:00, and child3.xml had 21 collections at 14:41:07-08. Live 2026-10-13: sitemap_products_1.xml has 185/185 at 2026-10-13T06:26:32+03:00, and the response Date is 03:27:31 GMT.

votes.reasoning: Two live fetches of sitemap_products_1.xml 4 seconds apart returned 185/185 products with lastmod 2026-10-13T06:26:28+03:00 and then 06:26:32+03:00. Product lastmod is the sitemap generation time, which is platform behaviour, not an app writing to products daily. The raw recommendation ('identify the writer, make syncs write only on change') is therefore wrong. Its falsifiability check (more than 20 distinct values within a week) can never pass. Google says lastmod is used only when it is 'consistently and verifiably accurate' and otherwise ignored, with no penalty. The cost is the loss of a freshness hint for products only. Articles and collections now show varied values. Low is right; the report-level Medium is inflated.
votes.corrected_recommendation: Document this as Shopify platform behaviour with no merchant action. Rely on article/collection lastmod and on internal linking for product recrawls. Optionally re-check in a few months whether Shopify changes it. Remove the 'find the writer' task from the action plan.

votes.reasoning: The finding is correct. Google's merchant listing documentation requires an Offer (AggregateOffer is accepted only for product snippets) and a numeric price with a dot decimal separator. '8,50' and '145,00' are invalid, so all 185 products are ineligible for merchant listings: High is right. The staging fix (one Offer per variant, price via divided_by: 100.0 | json, priceCurrency, availability, itemCondition, priceValidUntil) is valid Liquid and is safe. It needs one refinement for the 106 multi-variant products. The staging snippet puts the FIRST variant's sku and gtin at Product level while the offers array carries other variants with different prices and GTINs. On baton, that is the gtin of the 100 RON box next to an 8.5 RON offer. Google's Product variants documentation (ProductGroup + hasVariant + variesBy + productGroupID) is the intended model for this. The ambiguity can also cause price/identifier mismatches with the Simprosys Merchant Center feed when Merchant Center applies automatic item updates. Shopify's native structured_data filter already emits ProductGroup for multi-variant products. The specialist's suggestion to emit priceSpecification/StrikethroughPrice should not be applied (see SCHEMA-19), and staging correctly leaves it out.

findings.title: Colour/flavour variants published as separate products prevent ProductGroup markup
findings.evidence: Validator Info no-product-group on every MNX product; 19 near-duplicate title groups / 45 products (MNX colours, Frutilu flavours) published as separate products, so ProductGroup/variesBy/hasVariant cannot be expressed.

votes.reasoning: The fact holds: about 45 sibling colour and flavour products are separate products with no ProductGroup markup. The premise that this prevents ProductGroup is wrong. Google's product-variant markup supports multi-page setups where each variant has its own URL: a ProductGroup with a shared productGroupID and variesBy, plus hasVariant entries that point to each sibling URL. Merging products, which the owner rejected as DESIGN, is therefore not required.
votes.evidence: catalog-analysis: 19 near-duplicate title groups / 45 products. No ProductGroup in any local product page.

No design or URL change is needed.

votes.reasoning: The premise is too strong. Google's Product variants documentation explicitly supports a multi-page setup: variants on separate URLs, each page carrying ProductGroup markup with a shared productGroupID, variesBy (color/flavour) and hasVariant entries that link to each sibling URL. So keeping MNX colours and Frutilu flavours as separate products does not prevent ProductGroup markup. Merging them is not needed for schema. Round 2 classed the merge as DESIGN because it changes pages and URLs, and that is correct for a merge, but the markup route is invisible and needs no design change. The impact is low (variant understanding in Shopping and merchant listings), so Low is fine.

In the Product snippet, when the metafield exists, emit isVariantOf a ProductGroup {productGroupID, name, variesBy: https://schema.org/color (or a flavour property), hasVariant: [the sibling Product URLs]}, following Google's multi-page variant example. Validate on one MNX tee in the Rich Results Test. Merging stays an optional catalogue decision; if it is done, it needs 301s from the old product URLs.

votes.reasoning: The fields that carry no risk, priceValidUntil and itemCondition NewCondition, are already in the staging snippet. The StrikethroughPrice recommendation is unsafe as written. A strikethrough price in markup (and Google's sale-price annotations) must reflect a genuine earlier price. Under the EU Omnibus rules (Directive 2019/2161, as transposed in Romania), an announced price reduction must reference the lowest price of the previous 30 days. Round 2 found 120 products with permanent compare-at prices, so marking them up as StrikethroughPrice would amplify a likely non-compliant display into Google surfaces. Round 2 was right to leave it out. Low is fine.
votes.evidence: Staging schema-product-enhanced.liquid lines 101-102 (priceValidUntil, itemCondition). round2-status.md §3: SCHEMA-19 left out deliberately because of Omnibus risk.
votes.corrected_recommendation: Do not emit StrikethroughPrice from compare_at_price. Only once compare-at values represent the real lowest price of the previous 30 days (for genuine, time-limited promotions only) should a UnitPriceSpecification with priceType https://schema.org/StrikethroughPrice be added, and only for those variants. Otherwise remove permanent compare-at prices (commercial/legal decision for the owner).

Only the /ro-hu homepage and one /ro-hu product page were fetched live (8 of 15 allowed requests, no 429); the other 573 duplicates were assessed from the sitemap and Shopify's deterministic market rendering.

No test order was placed; checkout behaviour for Hungarian addresses (HUF rate conversion, tax lines) is inferred from Admin API delivery-profile and tax settings.

votes.reasoning: There were 78 auto-generated creatine articles for 3 products, with each intent written 3-11 times. This is the pattern Google's spam policies call scaled content abuse: many pages generated mainly to rank, not to help users. It also drags on site-wide helpfulness signals, so High is justified, and the risk goes beyond simple cannibalisation. The fix (one URL per intent, 301 the rest) matches Google's redirect guidance for consolidating content. It is admin-feasible through Shopify URL redirects. A redirect to a non-equivalent page is at worst treated as a soft 404, which is harmless here. Fixed on 2026-10-13 (round 2): the creatina hub went from 71 to 11 kept articles, with 60 redirects aimed at final handles, so there are no chains. Live: /blogs/news/gymbeam-creatine-creatina-monohidrat-micronized-300g-fara-5 returns a single 301 to /blogs/news/cum-se-ia-creatina, which returns 200. sitemap_articles_1.xml now lists 121 articles, of which 14 contain 'creatin'. The site: part of the falsifiability check is weak, since Google documents site: as non-exhaustive. The curl -sI over the redirected sources is the meaningful test, and so is the GSC query-to-page check.

votes.reasoning: Reproduced at audit time: 9 tagged articles and 5 tags (preworkout 3, arderea grasimilor 2, longevitate 2, sanatate 2, aminoacizi 1); 346 untagged; 11 per page. The round-2 claim (PARȚIAL) only partly holds and introduced a regression. Round 2 wrote hub:/intent:/produs: tags on every article, and the LIVE theme's blog filter bar now renders all of them as visible chips with raw labels. Each one is a 200, self-canonical, indexable /blogs/news/tagged/* page (live theme has no tag noindex; that fix is only READY-R2 on staging) that repeats the blog title. This is a visible change to the live design, against the owner's rule, and it creates about 180 thin duplicate-title URLs.
votes.evidence: Live /blogs/news?cb= (2026-10-13): 180 distinct /blogs/news/tagged/ links: intent 106, produs 51, hub 11, topic 12. Visible labels e.g. 'hub:creatina', 'intent:altele:gatit-cu-proteina', 'produs:ashwagandha-ksm-66'. Live /blogs/news/tagged/intent-altele-gatit-cu-proteina: 200, canonical self, no meta robots, <title>Blog despre suplimente și antrenament | Prime Supplements, 1 article (gatit-cu-pudra-proteica). theme-fixes/layout/theme.liquid lines 56-58 add noindex when current_tags is set, but no staging file filters internal tags out of the bar.

votes.reasoning: The original finding was correct: 5 tags on 9 articles and no taxonomy. The recommendation was sound on the key point, 'exactly one hub tag per article, keep the tag count at 12', but the remediation did not follow it, and the live site now has a regression. Each kept article got 4-5 tags (human topic, hub:, intent:, produs:), 181 distinct in total. Because sections/main-blog has show_tags enabled, the live /blogs/news filter bar and every tag page now show 180 visible chips: 106 'intent:…' (e.g. 'intent:comparatie:bcaa-vs-eaa'), 51 'produs:…', 11 'hub:…' and only 12 human ones. Cards show badges such as 'hub:vitamine-si-minerale'. Each chip is an indexable, self-canonical /blogs/news/tagged/<tag> URL with the same title as the blog index ('Blog despre suplimente și antrenament | Prime Supplements') and no robots meta (verified on /tagged/hub-creatina and /tagged/produs-pure-isolate-2000g). That is about 180 thin, duplicate-titled listing URLs next to roughly 330 indexable content URLs. Google's faceted-navigation guidance (Dec 2024) recommends keeping such low-value filter URLs out of crawling or indexing. It is also a visible UI change, which contradicts the owner's 'do not change the design' rule. Other parts of the recommendation need correcting. Shopify tag pages cannot have their own title or copy without theme work, and the staging theme (TECH-08, READY-R2) deliberately noindexes /tagged/ pages, so the collections with custom.hub_articles, not the tag pages, should be the editorial hubs. 'Raise articles_per_page to 24' is a design change (DESIGN per the owner).

Live /blogs/news/tagged/produs-pure-isolate-2000g: 200, title = blog title, no meta robots, self-canonical. blog-consolidation.json: 181 distinct tags.

Then publish the TECH-08 noindex,follow on /blogs/news/tagged/*. findings.title: Blog is scaled, unreviewed generator output on YMYL topics (scaled content abuse exposure)
findings.evidence: 347/355 bodies carry the BlogGenAI HTML comment, injected JSON-LD, 312 <style> blocks, 309 onclick handlers, 347 non-JSON-LD scripts. Velocity: 127 articles in 2026-05 (ISO W20: 46), 10 on 2026-05-15, 7-9/day on 14 other days. Identical template everywhere: 'Key Takeaways' 321, 'Share/Post' 349, 'Top 5 probleme pe care X le rezolvă' 299, in-body price cards 533 (median 2/article), arrow CTAs 1,825 (median 6/article). Unfilled prompt placeholder jobTitle 'Professional title based on niche' in 26 published Person JSON-LD blocks (15 in Sept 2026). 349 bodies open with English 'Published: May 15, 2026'; one published English-title article (fat-burner-x10-pareri-l-carnitine-1000-80-caps) and an unpublished all-English draft; 191 handles contain English prompt fragments; off-topic piece tricou-sala-cele-mai-bune-tricouri-yoga bylined 'Nutriționist Certificat'. No first-hand signals in any sampled 2026 body; content_quality.py (English lexicon) scores them 79-87 on density only.
findings.recommendation: Pause BlogGenAuto scheduling now; triage all 347 generated articles into keep-and-rewrite (~110-130), merge+301 (~190) and delete+301 using the CONTENT-05 cluster map (Shopify URL redirects, bulk CSV); for every kept article do a human editorial pass by the named author, strip generator chrome (price cards, CTAs, 'Top 5', English labels) and add an AI-assistance/review disclosure line; cap cadence at 4-6 reviewed articles/week.

limitations: No Search Console, analytics or SERP data: impact is inferred from content properties, not measured; indexation status of the 354 articles is unknown.

Plugin scorers (content_quality.py, content_verify.py, content_humanize.py) use English lexicons; their numbers are reported but the Romanian-language assessment relies on direct reading and deterministic regex scans. All scores are heuristics, not Google signals.
15 of 355 bodies were read in full or in part; corpus-wide numbers come from scans of all 355, but qualitative judgements are sampled.

Medical accuracy was assessed for plausibility and sourcing only; a clinician should review YMYL pieces before republication. Author credentials (NPC PRO cards, FRCF lecturer, 'Nutriționist Certificat') were not verified against any registry.

Generator <style> blocks and inline styles survive in 55 of the 121 repaired article bodies (applied/article-bodies/final). The generator layout is not fully stripped, even though JSON-LD, scripts and H1s were removed.

After round 2, none of the 121 live articles cites a primary source: 0 PubMed, PMC or DOI links in the final bodies. The only sourced pieces are 11 unpublished drafts, so the public YMYL blog still has no citations at all.

Person.jobTitle inconsistency was worse than reported: at least 10 distinct generator titles (for example 'Antrenor de culturism și nutriționist sportiv' 47, 'Expert Nutriție Sportivă și Biohacking' 42, 'Expert Nutriție Sportivă & Biohacking' 41, plus the 26 placeholder entries). Three of the six 2025 'human' articles were silently rewritten by BlogGenAI ('UpdatedOldBlog') and stamped 'Actualizat: 12 martie 2026'.

Round 2's product verification ('title, description and every tab text present in HTML', round2-status §4) can pass when the text appears only in <meta name=twitter:description> and the Product JSON-LD. On /products/creatina-monohidrat-micronized-300g-fara-aroma the new description, including the mandatory EU statements 'A nu se depăși doza zilnică recomandată' and 'nu înlocuiesc o dietă variată', is not visible. The default template disables both the 'description' block and the collapsible 'Descriere' block (recon templates__product.json). Re-verify all 85 supplements with a visible-text extraction.

The live theme still emits the hidden creatina FAQPage JSON-LD with unauthorised, diacritic-free claims ('cel mai studiat si eficient supliment pentru performanta sportiva'). Removing it is only READY-R2, so this health-claim leak stays live until the staging theme is published.

The live product BreadcrumbList puts position 2 on 'Cele mai vândute' (/collections/cele-mai-vandute), which is now seo.hidden (noindex,nofollow). The breadcrumb points users and Google to a noindexed utility collection until the staging breadcrumb snippet is published.

The 121 kept article bodies contain zero outbound citations (all decorative links removed), while 92 still say 'studiile/cercetările arată'. Removing the fake sources without adding real ones leaves unsourced YMYL claims; the 11 sourced drafts are unpublished.

The prime-health hub keeps 16 articles on medical conditions (cholesterol, blood pressure and similar) whose only named author is now openly described as a bodybuilding coach. Honest, but it is a YMYL expertise mismatch: consider unpublishing or obtaining a named health-professional review.
The staging About page text keeps the unverified 'TÜV, IFS, HALAL și Cologne List for Athletes' certification claim; publishing the theme would re-publish it in its newly 'verified' form.

seo.hidden on utility collections emits noindex,nofollow (not noindex,follow), so links on those listing pages are not followed. Harmless here because products are linked elsewhere, but worth noting next to the staging theme's noindex,follow logic.

results.score_rationale: Delivery mechanics are mostly right (Shopify CDN WebP negotiation confirmed live, srcset/sizes and width/height on theme images, native lazy-loading, fetchpriority=high on the hero) and keep the category off the floor. The 1,024-byte point therefore has no user or Google impact. The second point, a parser-blocking script, does not change after the fix either, because the recommendation correctly keeps Pandectes synchronous: consent tools must run before pixels. What remains is hygiene that duplicates TECH-09, so Low, not Medium. (b) The staged order (charset, viewport, title/meta/canonical, JSON-LD, Pandectes, ..., content_for_header) is valid Liquid and keeps Pandectes ahead of every app script, so it is safe. (c) 'curl | head -c 1024 | grep -c meta charset == 1' is meaningful. 'Lighthouse charset passes' is not, because it already passes on the HTTP header.

votes.reasoning: (a) The measurement is right. The main cost is main-thread parse and execution, which feeds INP and TBT. There is also a compounding effect the report does not state: inline scripts placed after the Fontify stylesheets cannot run until those cross-origin CSS files load, which holds up the parser. The claim that this delays 'LCP discovery' is overstated, because Chrome's preload scanner reads ahead and the whole document is ~82 KB brotli. With no CrUX/INP data and Google's position that CWV is one signal among many, this is Medium, not High. Scope is now ~360 URLs, not 1,151. (b) Several suggested actions are risky or not under the merchant's control. Judge.me's jdgmSettings comes from the global core embed, which also powers the star badges on collection/homepage cards and the homepage carousel. Merchants cannot scope an app embed per template, and turning it off breaks badges. Moving theMarketer to GTM 'after consent' can break its feed and attribution and must be validated with the vendor. Shopify's web-pixels-manager and Monorail blocks (~20-30 KB) are platform output that cannot be removed. The safe levers: uninstall apps with no business value (Estimator if unused, UpPromote/Secomapp if no affiliates, Pop Convert, BlogGenAuto, which round 2 says must be stopped anyway), disable unused Judge.me widgets (Q&A, floating tab), and limit Pandectes languages. (c) A head target under 80 KB is not reachable because of platform inline code; a realistic bar is under 110 KB. Field INP p75 from Shopify's Web performance report is the meaningful check.

limitations: No lab or field Core Web Vitals: PSI (anonymous quota exhausted), CrUX, GSC and Lighthouse/Chromium were unavailable in the sandbox; no LCP/INP/CLS values, TBT, waterfall or main-thread profile exist. All LCP-element and main-thread statements are static inferences; the score carries roughly +/-10 points of uncertainty and should be re-based on Shopify's Web performance report or GSC CWV data once 28 days of traffic exist.
TTFB measured once from a US edge (IAD) with curl; it indicates server health, not Romanian user experience.
layout/theme.liquid was not in the theme dump ($R/theme/ holds 15 files, no layout file); head-order recommendations are based on rendered HTML and Impact's known structure.

Barlow font-file byte totals were not fetched (live-request budget); Poppins weights actually downloaded by a browser depend on the weights used by the overridden selectors (expected 400/500/600/700), not on the 54 declared faces.
Image transfer sizes measured with a Chrome Accept header (WebP); AVIF may be somewhat smaller for newer browsers.
Product template assessed on one supplement product (baton-proteic-capsuni); MNX apparel pages with 24-39 gallery images share the same head/app stack but have heavier galleries.
Live requests to the store were capped at 15 (2 s apart, no 429 encountered); the recommended request-count and byte targets are design goals, not measured baselines.

missed_issues: Live state change since the audit, worth checking under 'do not break anything': the live homepage of 2026-10-13 prints 'Failed to render app block "6770548097779500122": app block path shopify://apps/koala-upsells-gifts/blocks/gifts-embed/... does not exist', and gifts-embed.js (120 KB) no longer loads. The same happens for the BlogGenAuto tracking-embed. round2-status §5 says Koala Gifts is active on the live theme and should be re-enabled before publishing, but on live it is already gone. The owner should confirm the gift/upsell feature was switched off on purpose, then remove the orphaned embeds.

On article pages, the related-article blog-post-card images (4000x2667 sources) render with no sizes attribute and no loading=lazy (loading_strategy stays nil because no position is passed and section.index <= 3). The browser assumes 100vw and eagerly fetches about 2000 px renditions (112 KB WebP each, 2 per article) below the fold. The specialist mislabelled these as in-body images, and theme-fixes does not change blog-post-card.

Broken in-body image: https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0917/5138/3415/files/silicoane-mai-mari.png?v=1773333647 returns 404 but is still in the live /blogs/news/bcaa-vs-eaa body after the round-2 re-import. The import validator kept images without checking that their URLs resolve.

Five render-blocking stylesheets in <head> on every template: theme.css (27 KB), bss-custom.css (only 192 B br, a whole request for a tiny file that could be inlined), two Google Fonts CSS files, and Judge.me shopify_v2.css (14.5 KB). Only customer-referral.css and country-flags.css are loaded non-blocking.

No finding states the decisive baseline gap: whether primesupplements.ro has any CrUX data at all (origin or URL level). Google's CWV ranking input comes only from CrUX field data, so if there is none, the High ratings for PERFORMANCE-01/03/04/05 have no Search effect to point to. The action plan should start with checking CrUX (PSI with an API key, or the CrUX dashboard) and Shopify Admin > Web performance (RUM LCP/INP/CLS) before re-prioritising.

BlogGenAuto is still publishing. The live article /blogs/news/cum-alegi-crema-de-orez (images dated 2026-10-10/11, listed first on the blog index on 2026-10-13) again carries in-body Article/FAQPage/BreadcrumbList/Person JSON-LD, an extra in-body <style> block (.related-posts-grid with !important), in-body images without width/height or srcset, and the full commerce app stack. The round-2 body clean-up does not protect new posts, so stopping the app is a performance and markup prerequisite, not only a content issue.

Publishing the staging theme carries a regression risk for performance and functionality. Round 2 §5 says Shopify removed the Koala Gifts embed from the staging settings_data on API write. Publishing without re-enabling it silently breaks gift-with-purchase. Re-enabling it brings back the 120 KB gifts-embed.js, so before/after measurements must account for it.

Script-blocking CSS interaction, missing from both PERFORMANCE-01 and -03: the ~60 inline head scripts that follow the Fontify Google Fonts stylesheets cannot execute until those cross-origin stylesheets have loaded, so the font CSS delays HTML parsing as well as rendering. This is the strongest argument for at least adding a fonts.gstatic.com preconnect and limiting the Poppins weights now.

findings.title: Freshness signals are fabricated: hard-coded 'Published:' lines disagree with Shopify dates, 'Updated' always equals 'Published', 267/354 articles older than 90 days, two conflicting Article schemas per page
findings.evidence: 348/354 bodies start with literal English 'Published: <date> | Updated: <same date>'; 315 disagree with Shopify publishedAt (219 by -1 day, 52 by -7, 44 by -30); Updated==Published 348/348; Shopify updatedAt differs from publishedAt in only 29 articles; age at 2026-10-12: 87 <=90d, 219 at 91-180d, 48 >180d; 279/355 titles contain 2025/2026, 352 bodies say 'în 2026'. article-2026-citicolina.html has 6 ld+json blocks incl. two Article entities: BlogGenAI (datePublished 2026-04-14T02:20:02.026Z, author Person) and theme snippets__schema-article.liquid (2026-04-14T05:20:02+0300, author Organization 'Prime Supplements').

Overstated parts: the two Article entities on article-2026-citicolina.html carry the SAME instant (2026-04-14T02:20:02Z = 05:20:02+03:00), so they conflict only on author type (Person vs Organization), not on dates; 'în 2026' appears in 338 bodies, not 352; being older than 90 days is not a fabrication signal. votes.reasoning: The core defect was real. The body text showed a date that disagreed with Shopify's date, 'Updated' always equalled 'Published', and two Article entities with different authors and dates appeared on one page. Google's byline-date guidance asks for one clear visible date that matches datePublished/dateModified. Google's helpful-content guide warns against 'changing the date of pages to make them seem fresh when the content has not substantially changed'. Three points are inflated. First, 219 of the 315 mismatches are off by exactly one day, which is a UTC-vs-+03:00 artefact rather than fabrication. Second, '267 articles older than 90 days' is not a defect for evergreen content. Third, a wrong byline date mostly affects date display and CTR, not ranking, so Medium fits better than High. Two parts of the fix are unsafe. Binding a visible 'Actualizat la' date to article.updated_at is wrong, because updated_at changes on any admin edit (tags, metafields, bulk imports); the 13.10 body import already set dateModified to 2026-10-13 on all 121 articles. The '>30% updated_at > published_at+30d' falsifiability is gameable and now passes trivially, so it is not meaningful.

results.score_rationale: In 11 Romanian commercial SERPs observed on 2026-10-12 (pudra proteica, proteine din zer, suplimente pre workout, batoane proteice, arzator de grasimi, cea mai buna creatina, suplimente culturism, creatina creapure, prime whey, pre workout fara cofeina, bcaa vs eaa) primesupplements.ro never appeared; restricted to Romanian stores it surfaces only with 2026 blog posts for creatina/creatina monohidrata while gymbeam.ro, bodyline.ro and decathlon.ro rank with category and product pages. The brand name is not owned in search (Hagen Prime, Blackstone Prime Nutrition, QNT/Prozis Prime Whey), legacy WooCommerce URLs and the B2B store are still indexed, and the home/collection/product/article templates fail the skeptical and price-comparing personas (P3 scores 28/28/48/29). SXO Gap Scores: /collections/creatina 38, /collections/pudra-proteica 40, BCAA article 35, creatina-creapure product 58.
what_works: Main store is indexed with Romanian keyword-led titles on key collections (site: results: 'Pudra proteica pentru masa musculară', 'Suplimente Pre Workout pentru energie maximă', 'Vitamine și minerale esențiale', 'Despre noi - Prime Supplements', EAA and Frutilu product pages).

The domain can rank: /blogs/news/creatina-monohidrata-nitrox-no-stim-combining-supplements, /blogs/news/monohydrate-creatine-cum-sa-stii-daca-creatina and /blogs/news/creatina-si-volumizarea-musculara-cum-sa-stii-daca-creatina appeared next to gymbeam.ro/decathlon.ro/bodyline.ro in the store-restricted creatina checks.

Product buy box is complete for decision-stage buyers: 'Preț redus 180,00 lei', 'În stoc', 'Produs în Uniunea Europeană', 2 variants, '17 recenzii', 'Adaugă în coș' + 'Cumpără acum', site-wide 'Livrare gratuită la comenzile de peste 300 RON', payment methods listed in the FAQ.

Collections already expose filters (Doar în stoc, Preț, Cantitate) and 8 sort options; the Impact theme main-collection section can host description/rich-text blocks, so the fix is content not development.
Blog corpus is long-form (median 1529 words, 348/355 with tables, 338 citing studies, median 10 product links per article): raw material for consolidation into category hubs.
limitations: WebSearch is a US-indexed engine, not google.ro: no PAA, ads, AI Overview, shopping units or related searches were observable; bare Romanian queries (creatina, creatina monohidrata pret, glutamina, pre workout, bcaa vs eaa diferente, creatina creapure) returned Spanish/Portuguese/French/Italian pages and were complemented with qualified or store-restricted variants. 'Absent' means absent from this engine's top results on 2026-10-12, strong but not conclusive for google.ro.
The site: operator was only partially honoured (site:primesupplements.ro/ro-hu returned unrelated domains), so index coverage counts are indicative.
No Search Console, GA4, CrUX or rank-tracking data; personas and user stories were derived from SERP result composition rather than PAA/ad copy.

Only one collection (/collections/pudra-proteica), one product (/products/creatina-creapure) and one article (BCAA vs EAA) were scored in depth; systemic patterns were verified across parsed files but per-page scores for other URLs may differ.
Pages were assessed from static HTML copies, not a rendered viewport; above-the-fold order is inferred from section order in the HTML (plugin render/fetch scripts fail in this sandbox).

In each remaining article add a first-screen link to /collections/creatina and a product card via article.metafields.custom.featured_product in sections/main-article.liquid. Remove duplicate primesupplements1.myshopify.com links.
findings.falsifiability: After 8-12 weeks GSC Pages filtered on queries containing 'creatin' should show /collections/creatina and the creatine products as top URLs; if blog URLs still take >70% of creatine impressions the consolidation failed.

The SERP log came from a US-indexed WebSearch engine, not google.ro, and the specialist's own scope note says it returned no Romanian PAA or shopping data and gave non-Romanian results for plain queries. The structural problem is real: 68 creatine-titled articles against a 3-product collection with an empty description. It is also largely a subset of SXO-09 (cannibalisation), so I downgrade it to Medium. Round 2: blog consolidation is live, so the part the PARȚIAL state claims holds.
votes.evidence: From $R/shopify/articles-all.json: 68/355 titles contain 'creatin', 80 handles contain it, 19 handles contain 'creapure' and 42 handles end in -2..-5. One gap: the live creatine collection's 'Ghiduri' block still shows crema-de-orez articles, because the hub block is staging-only.

votes.reasoning: (a) The finding is real and matters. When posts rather than the category/product pages rank for transactional creatine queries, the store has an intent mismatch, and Google's helpful-content and e-commerce guidance expects category pages to serve shopping intent. Two things lower the severity. First, the SERP evidence came from a US-indexed WebSearch with store-restricted queries, not google.ro (sxo.md admits this), so 'the pages Google associates' is an inference. Second, the cannibalisation half is the same issue as SXO-09/CLUSTER-04, which is now FIXED-R2. What remains is collection strength, which fits Medium. (b) Three parts of the fix need correcting. A 'Judge.me aggregate for the collection' may be shown on the page but must not be marked up as AggregateRating on a collection page: Google's review-snippet guidelines require ratings about a specific item, not a category or list. A SKU comparison table with preț/porție hard-coded in collection.description goes stale and will contradict the Offer price and the Merchant feed, so it should be rendered in Liquid from variant.price. The article product card via a metafield block in main-article.liquid is a visible template change, which breaks the owner's no-design rule. In-body contextual links do the same job as a data change. The '8 pillars' target is overtaken by the R2 consolidation (121 kept, one per intent). (c) The falsifiability check (GSC share of 'creatin' impressions on /collections or /products versus blog, >70% threshold) is measurable once GSC is connected. GSC is not configured yet.

votes.reasoning: (a) This is a genuine on-page gap, but 'High' overstates it. Google does not require long copy on category pages, and the category competitors named (decathlon.ro, drmax.ro, emag.ro) rank with grid-first pages and little text. Their advantage is authority and assortment, not a 700-word block. Under the audit rules, thin collection copy is an optimisation, so Medium. (b) The 300-700-word target with 3-5 FAQs per collection risks boilerplate SEO text under the grid. FAQ markup has no SERP effect since May 2026, so the FAQs are content only. The Cantitate filter fix is a valid Search & Discovery task: filter values come from variant option values, so option names such as 'Cantitate' and 'Gramaj' must be unified on the products, which is a data change, not a design change. Google follows up to 10 redirect hops, and a few stale site: rows are cosmetic: Google documents site: as neither complete nor representative of what ranks. Nothing here 'materially hurts rankings on many pages', so Low. (b) Two parts of the fix are wrong or unsafe. 'Add redirects for the observed ?v= variants' cannot be done: Shopify URL redirects fire only when the path 404s and cannot match query strings on live paths. 'Use Removals > Outdated content for the www/legacy results' contradicts Google's documentation. The Removals tool should not be used to clean up URLs after a site move or redirect, and Outdated Content is meant for third-party pages. A temporary removal also covers the http/https and www/non-www variants, so a mistaken prefix removal on www.primesupplements.ro/ would hide the live non-www site. The redirect-map part is done (25 /categorie-produs/* rules are now single-hop). (c) 'site:... categorie-produs returns 0' is an unreliable signal. findings.title: The wholesale store b2b.primesupplements.ro is indexed and surfaces product pages with B2B prices to consumers
findings.evidence: site:b2b.primesupplements.ro returned https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/combat-pro 'Combat PRO 500g/22 serv' showing 140 RON vs 170 RON, flavours, 'pickup unavailable', seller PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL. Live HTTP 200, no noindex, no canonical to the main store; the B2B sitemap lists 58 product URLs with the same handles as the main store ($R/pages/b2b-products-sitemap.xml).
findings.affected_scope: 58 B2B product URLs duplicating 58 retail products (31% of the catalogue).
findings.recommendation: Put the B2B store behind login (Shopify B2B 'require customers to log in' / storefront password), add <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> in its layout/theme.liquid, remove it from sitemap submission; if it must stay public add <link rel="canonical" href="https://primesupplements.ro/products/{{ product.handle }}"> on its product template. Keep /pages/inregistrare-b2b on the main domain as the only indexable B2B entry.
findings.falsifiability: site:b2b.primesupplements.ro returns 0 results within 4-8 weeks; otherwise the noindex is not served on the fetched pages.
findings.leading_indicator: GSC coverage of the b2b property; B2B order source mix.

votes.reasoning: The B2B store is indexable, and its product pages self-canonicalise on the b2b domain. The counts are slightly off: the B2B sitemap has 57 product URLs, and 52 of those handles match active retail products. The Combat PRO SERP example comes from the non-Google engine, but the indexability is reproducible. This is still pending as an owner action.
votes.evidence: $R/pages/b2b-product.html has no robots meta, and its canonical is https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/creatina-creapure (self, not the main store). $R/pages/b2b-products-sitemap.xml has 58 <loc> entries, of which 57 are /products/ URLs. 52 of the 57 handles match the 185 active main-store handles (28%, not 31%). No live re-check (request budget).

votes.reasoning: (a) This matters. Fifty-eight product pages (31% of the catalogue) are duplicated cross-domain with different prices, 140 vs 170 RON. Google picks one URL per duplicate cluster, and the wholesale page can be chosen as canonical, so consumers see B2B pricing and the retail page loses the snippet. That is the same root issue as TECH-02 (High), so High stands. (b) The direction is right, with three corrections. Use 'noindex' alone; 'nofollow' adds nothing. Do not combine noindex with a cross-domain canonical. Google advises against mixing those signals, and with different prices the canonical may be ignored anyway, so noindex is the reliable path. Do not block b2b in robots.txt until the pages have dropped out, because Google must crawl them to see the noindex. 'Require customers to log in' for Shopify B2B is a Plus feature. On a non-Plus store the options are the storefront password (shared with approved clients) or a theme-level login gate, which is the owner's business decision. 'Remove it from sitemap submission' just means not submitting it in GSC, since the Shopify sitemap is auto-generated. The retail-site links to the B2B storefront should point to the main-domain /pages/inregistrare-b2b instead. (c) Falsifiability: 'site:b2b returns 0' is approximate. URL Inspection on the b2b property ('Excluded by noindex tag') and a GSC Pages count are better.
votes.evidence: Live 13.10 page5: canonical https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/products/combat-pro, no <meta name=robots>, ProductGroup JSON-LD valid. Retail homepage/article HTML: href="https://b2b.primesupplements.ro" and href="https://b2b.primesupplements.ro/pages/inregistrare-b2b".

Do not add a cross-domain canonical in addition to the noindex. Optionally gate the store (storefront password, or B2B login if on Plus). Point retail-site B2B links to https://primesupplements.ro/pages/inregistrare-b2b. Verify the b2b property in GSC and track 'Excluded by noindex tag' for the 58 product URLs over 4-8 weeks.

findings.title: Commercial head-term SERPs are dominated by pharmacies, medical publishers and marketplaces; the store competes with zero authority and no advertorial/PR footprint
findings.evidence: Recurrent ranking domains across 11 commercial queries: drmax.ro (8), bulk.com/ro (5), medlife.ro (4), decathlon.ro (3), gymbeam.ro (2), catena.ro, biogena.com, emag.ro, worldclass.ro, bzi.ro advertorials for Bodyline x2 ('Prima pagină » Magazin » Bodyline. findings.falsifiability: No new referring domains in 6 months and no movement on the 11 queries shows the authority gap was not addressed.
findings.leading_indicator: Referring domains count; GSC impressions on non-brand category queries.

votes.reasoning: The SERP domain tallies come from a US-indexed engine that returned non-Romanian pages for plain Romanian queries. 'primesupplements.ro 0 of 11' is therefore not evidence about google.ro. The authority gap (domain absent from the Common Crawl web graph) is established in the context file. What remains is generic PR and authority advice, so Low.
votes.evidence: The Common Crawl graph absence is confirmed in audit-context.md. The SERP composition can't be reproduced in this sandbox: no google.ro and no rank tracker, and the specialist's scope section says plain queries returned ES/PT/FR/IT pages.

votes.reasoning: (a) The observation is largely a market condition (pharmacies, medical publishers and marketplaces dominate YMYL-flavoured supplement SERPs), and it was gathered on a US-indexed engine. It is real context for priorities but generic, and the 'zero authority' claim rests on Common Crawl absence, not link data. It fits Medium as a strategic note, not a defect. (b) One part of the fix breaks a Google policy. '4-6 Romanian advertorials ... linking to collection hubs' is a link scheme unless the links carry rel="sponsored" (or nofollow). Google's spam policies name 'advertorials or native advertising where payment is received for articles that include links that pass ranking credit'. Paid placements buy visibility and brand demand, not PageRank. 'Cea mai bună creatină în 2026' reintroduces the year-bait titles that round 2 removed. The lab-transparency page with per-batch certificates is the strongest item: it supports YMYL trust for P3 and is safe. Price aggregators (compari.ro, price.ro) need a product feed and are fine. (c) 'No new referring domains in 6 months' measures effort, not outcome. Pair it with GSC impressions on the 11 non-brand category queries.

results.score_rationale: Weighted per the seo-ecommerce skill (schema 25% -> 10, title/meta 15% -> 35, images 20% -> 30, content 20% -> 35, internal linking 10% -> 30, technical 10% -> 55). The store cannot earn product rich results or a clean Merchant Center feed today: Product JSON-LD is invalid on multi-line descriptions and uses AggregateOffer with comma prices on all 185 products, productType is empty on 185/185, vendor is the myshopify handle on 64, 27 published GTINs fail the check digit, 79 products have no meta description at all, and the indexable /ro-hu duplicates show prices without 21% VAT. Foundations are sound (canonicalised facets, server-rendered Judge.me reviews, policy pages, valid UCP profile), so most fixes are data entry plus two Liquid snippets.

Every supplement sits in at least one real category collection; 69/85 supplement titles carry the pack size.
Featured images are large (none under 1024 px; 81 at 1500x1875, 43 at 4000x4000) and served as AVIF with descriptive filenames.

Product export lacks options, standard category, variant weights and Google-channel metafields; option names come from sampled HTML only (MNX exposes a single 'Size' option).

votes.reasoning: Google ignores JSON-LD that does not parse. AggregateOffer with comma-decimal strings also fails the Product snippet and Merchant listing rules, which need a numeric price in an Offer (Search Central, 'Merchant listing structured data'). That means no product rich-result eligibility anywhere on the site, which meets the audit's definition of Critical. The recommendation is right: use the json filter, one Offer per variant, a numeric price, shippingDetails, hasMerchantReturnPolicy, and aggregateRating from the reviews.* metafields. The falsifiability check is measurable: the Rich Results Test, json.load over every block, and the GSC Merchant listings report. I checked the staged implementation. It is valid Liquid, its GS1 check-digit loop is correct, seller @id matches the Organization @id, and microdata-schema stays commented out, so there is no duplicate Product. It has three defects. (1) returnFees is ReturnShippingFees without returnShippingFeesAmount. Google's MerchantReturnPolicy docs require the amount when that value is used. The return page says 'Va trebui să suportați costul direct al returnării', so the correct value is ReturnFeesCustomerResponsibility, which is what the specialist proposed. (2) strip_newlines joins words together in the description ('administrareDupă'). (3) Offer name prints 'Default Title' on single-variant products.
votes.corrected_recommendation:
Publish the staging theme, after re-enabling the Koala Gifts embed, or hot-patch the live snippet now. Changing the description line to `{{ product.description | strip_html | truncate: 500 | json }}`, without the surrounding quotes, is invisible and within the owner's no-design rule. Before publishing, fix the staged snippet: set returnFees to https://schema.org/ReturnFeesCustomerResponsibility (or add returnShippingFeesAmount if the shop charges a fixed fee); replace strip_newlines with `| replace: newline, ' '` after `{%- capture newline %}
{% endcapture -%}` (or strip_html after newline_to_br) so words are not joined; omit the Offer name when variant.title == 'Default Title'. Verify with the Rich Results Test on one supplement and one MNX URL.

votes.reasoning: Off-site reputation matters. Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines tell raters to research a site's reputation through independent sources, especially for YMYL-adjacent topics like supplements, and AI answer engines favour entities that are corroborated elsewhere. But the 'zero' evidence comes from a search tool that the specialist says is US-centric and ignores site:/exact-match operators (confidence 0.7). Every Romanian SRL is listed on registry aggregators (termene.ro, listafirme.ro), so '0 directories' is almost certainly a tool artefact. My termene.ro and Bing checks came back with a Cloudflare challenge and an empty page; that is a sandbox limitation, not evidence either way. With the evidence this uncertain, High is not justified. The recommendation also has a policy problem: it says to create a Google Business Profile and Bing Places listing for the 'Cisnădie office'. The local specialist (findings/local.md, LOCAL-11) established that the business is online-only, with no pickup and no customer-facing location. Google Business Profile guidelines make online-only businesses ineligible, and listing a registered office that receives no customers risks suspension. Listing on eMAG also has a side effect: the same product descriptions on a high-authority marketplace can outrank the store's own product pages.

votes.reasoning: The finding is real. The live Organization block is unchanged on 2026-10-13 because the staging theme is still unpublished: it has no address, telephone, email, legalName or vatID, and foundingDate is 2020. The severity is overstated, though. Google's Organization structured-data documentation says there are no required properties and that these fields only help Google understand the business. Leaving them out loses no rich result and has no measurable effect on rankings or CTR across many pages, so under the audit's own rules this is Medium, not High. The suggested Liquid is also unsafe. It builds JSON strings with `| escape`, the same mistake that made the Product and Article JSON-LD invalid (escape does not handle newlines and turns quotes into HTML entities). It also pulls shop.address.* while the store profile is incomplete: a read-back on 2026-10-13 shows city empty and street without a number, so it would output an empty addressLocality. The staging snippet (theme-fixes/snippets/schema-organization.liquid) avoids both problems by hard-coding values and using `| json`. Two problems remain in both the live and the staging block. First, the logo URL https://primesupplements.ro/cdn/shop/files/logo-prime-supplements.png returns 404 on both HEAD and GET, which breaks Google's logo requirement that the image be crawlable and indexable. Second, vatID is missing even though ANAF lists the company as a VAT payer. Staging also adds currenciesAccepted and paymentAccepted, which are LocalBusiness properties that are not valid on Organization/OnlineStore and only produce validator warnings. Minor scope error: the B2B store does have an Organization block (Impact's native one, named 'PRIME SPORT SUPPLEMENTS SRL / 46260823'). The falsifiability check (Rich Results Test shows Organization; grep PostalAddress = 1) is measurable.

The real header logo is cdn/shop/files/logo-prime-negru.svg. The staging snippet still points logo at the 404 URL. Admin read-back: shop.billingAddress city "", address1 'Strada Ioan Virgil Ispas'.

(2) Add "vatID": "RO46260823" next to taxID. (3) Remove currenciesAccepted and paymentAccepted. Keep the address values hard-coded, not from shop.address, until the owner completes the store profile (LOCAL-05). Keep `| json` on every Liquid value. Do not reuse the specialist's `| escape` snippet. Severity Medium.

findings.title: Cookie banner is a full-screen modal on mobile and hides the hero on desktop
findings.evidence: `visual/home-mobile.png`, `visual/product-creapure-mobile.png`, `visual/collection-creatina-mobile.png`, `visual/home-desktop.png`: the Pandectes consent dialog ("Acest site web folosește cookie-uri…", Accept / Preferințe) covers 100% of the 390x844 viewport and the centre 30% of the desktop hero. No content is readable until the visitor acts.
findings.affected_scope: every page, every first visit (mobile ≈ 70% of traffic for this vertical).
findings.recommendation: switch the Pandectes banner to a bottom sheet / compact bar (Pandectes → Banner → Layout "Bar" or "Box bottom-left"), keep "Accept"/"Reject" equal, and defer non-essential scripts until consent. Keep the H1 and hero CTA unobstructed.
